title: Insertion outside the p-monomial span preserves p-independence
statement: Let $K/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension], let $p$ be prime, and assume $k$ and $K$ have characteristic $p$. Put $F=kK^p$, the intermediate field generated by $k$ and all $p$-th powers in $K$. For a subset $T\subseteq K$, let $\mathcal M_p(T)$ consist of the finitely supported maps $E:T\to\mathbf N$ with $E(t)<p$ for all $t$, and write $t^E=\prod_{t\in T}t^{E(t)}$. If $(t^E)_{E\in\mathcal M_p(T)}$ is $F$-linearly independent and $x\in K$ lies outside its $F$-linear span, then the bounded monomials indexed by $\mathcal M_p(T\cup\{x\})$ are $F$-linearly independent.

source.place: More on Algebra, Definition Tag 07P1 (definition-p-basis) and Lemma Tag 07P2 (lemma-p-basis), third proof paragraph, maximal p-independent subsets; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07P2

proof.text: Put F = kK^p and M = span_F of the bounded monomials. For any finitely supported exponent function E, let D(t) = E(t) mod p and c = product (t^p)^(E(t)/p), regarded as an element of F. The exponent division identity gives the E-monomial as c times the D-monomial, hence every unrestricted monomial lies in M. Products of bounded monomials are the monomial indexed by the sum of their exponent functions. Two applications of span induction give multiplication closure. The zero exponent and singleton exponent give 1 and every t in T. Scalar multiplication gives all of F. For a nonzero element a of M, the scalar c=a^p belongs to F and a inverse equals c inverse times a^(p-1); for a=0 inverse is zero. Thus M is an intermediate field. Its universal property and membership of every bounded monomial in F(T) identify M with F(T). This is the fully proved private helper pMonomial_span_eq_adjoin.

Let L=F(T). The span equality makes x lie outside L. The element c=x^p belongs to F and therefore to L. If b^p=c for b in L, injectivity of Frobenius in the field K identifies b with x, contrary to x not in L. Apply the existing irreducibility leaf for X^p-C(c). This polynomial is monic, vanishes at x, and so equals minpoly L x by minpoly.eq_of_irreducible_of_monic. Its natural degree is p. Mathlib linearIndependent_pow, the independence consequence of the simple-extension power basis leaf, gives independence over L of the first p powers of x. This is the fully proved private helper pIndependent_powers_of_not_mem_span; it replaces the original coefficient-of-(X-x)^d argument.

The singleton exponent at any t in T shows t lies in the monomial span, hence x is outside T. Equiv.Set.insert identifies insert x T with T plus a singleton. Reindex each bounded exponent function by this equivalence, restrict to T using Finsupp.comapDomain, and read its exponent at the singleton to obtain an old bounded exponent and an element of Fin p. This splitting is injective by extensionality on the two summands. Finsupp.prod_equivMapDomain and Finsupp.prod_sumElim show that the new monomial is the old monomial times the corresponding power of x. Regard the old monomials as elements of L; they are F-independent by LinearIndependent.of_comp applied to the inclusion into K. Mathlib linearIndependent_smul gives F-independence of their products with the L-independent powers of x. Restrict along the injective splitting map by LinearIndependent.comp to conclude. This is the fully proved private helper pIndependent_insert_core, applied to the powers theorem.

theorem pIndependent_insert_of_not_mem_span
    {k : Type u} {K : Type v} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p] [CharP K p]
    (T : Set K)
    (hT : LinearIndependent
      (IntermediateField.adjoin k (Set.range (fun a : K ↦ a ^ p)))
      (fun E : {E : T →₀ ℕ // ∀ t : T, E t < p} ↦
        E.val.prod (fun t e ↦ (t : K) ^ e)))
    (x : K)
    (hx : x ∉ Submodule.span
      (IntermediateField.adjoin k (Set.range (fun a : K ↦ a ^ p)))
      (Set.range (fun E : {E : T →₀ ℕ // ∀ t : T, E t < p} ↦
        E.val.prod (fun t e ↦ (t : K) ^ e)))) :
    LinearIndependent (IntermediateField.adjoin k (Set.range (fun a : K ↦ a ^ p)))
      (fun E : {E : ↥(insert x T) →₀ ℕ // ∀ t : ↥(insert x T), E t < p} ↦
        E.val.prod (fun t e ↦ (t : K) ^ e))
